architecture.mechanism: A sine-wave curved carbon fiber composite (CFRP) structure with optimized ply-angle layup improves shaft-system operation by transmitting high torque (7.5 kN·m) while compensating axial displacement (4 mm), reducing the cyclic torsional/bending stress that drives shaft fracture.
architecture.intervention: Redesign the 2019 Chevrolet Silverado 1500 propeller shaft as a CFRP sine-wave curved tubular assembly laid up with the paper's optimized ply angles and fabricated by compression molding, replacing the fracture-prone steel shaft and its rigid coupling behavior.
architecture.expected_effect: Higher torque transmission capacity plus axial/misalignment compensation lowers peak stress and stress concentration at the shaft/coupling, preventing propeller shaft fracture and the resulting vehicle shake, thereby improving stability.
architecture.falsification_test: Bench-test the CFRP sine-wave curved propeller shaft against the original steel shaft under cyclic torque ramped to 7.5 kN·m with imposed axial displacement up to 4 mm, measuring strain, runout, and fatigue life; if the CFRP sine-wave shaft does not exceed the steel shaft in torque capacity, displacement compensation, and cycles-to-failure, the mechanism is falsified.
